(BY MS PRIYANKA JAIN - PANEL LAWYER FOR STATE)
 Th is appeal coming on for hearing this day, t h e cour  following:
 ORDER

This Criminal Appeal under Section 374(2) of Cr.P.C has been preferred feeling aggrieved by the judgment dated 22.06.2009, 03.07.2009 in S.T. No.20/2008 by Second Additional Session Judge,
Khandwa whereby the appellant No.1 Anand has been convicted for the offence punishable under Sections 366, 354, 342 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 4 years and fine of Rs.100/-, R.I.
for 2 years and R.I. for 1 year with default stipulations and appellant No.2 Shravan has been convicted for the offence 2 CRA-1291-2009 punishable under Section 342 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 1 year.
2. The prosecution case in nutshell before the Trial Court was that on 30.11.2007 at 3 PM the victim went on the well of the Village to wash her cloths.
She was in the requirement of a Bucket and for that she was going to the house of her uncle Bansilal.
In the way, appellant No.1 Anand caught hold the victim and brought her into the house of appellant No.2 Shravan and appellant No.2 Shravan locked the door from the out side.
The appellant No.1 Anand dashed down the victim and tried to rape.
She cried for help and on that her uncle's son Raghu and Mahendra (a villager) came there and

1 rescued the victim and brought to her home.

sentences.text: She narrated the incident to her father Bhim and after that the FIR was lodged in the Police Station, Mughat, District Khandwa.
FIR was registered as Crime No.598/2007 under Sections 354 and 342 read with 34 of the IPC against the appellants.
Victim was medically examined.

The appellants were arrested and after usual investigation, the charge sheet was filed before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Khandwa for the offence punishable under Sections 354, 342, 376 read with 511, 363 and 366-A of the IPC.
After committal, the case was submitted before the Trial Court.
3. Trail Court framed the charges for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376 read with 511 and 342 read with 34.
The appellants denied the allegations, abjured the guilt and payed for trial.
4. After recording the evidence of the prosecution, the trial Court examined the appellants, the appellants have submitted that they have falsely been implicated in the case.
They are innocent.
The appellants have not adduced any evidence on their behalf.
The trial Court after hearing the parties convicted the appellants as stated in para no.1 of the impugned judgment.

6. The trial Court regarding the appellant No.1 Anand call the report of the Probation Officer and after the judgment passed on 03.07.2009 considered the report of the Probation Officer and after that sentenced the appellant, hence, this appeal.
7. Learned counsel for the appellants has submitted that the appellants are innocent.
At the time of incident they were youth and 15 years have been elapsed since the appeal is pending.
The statement of the prosecutrix was only supported from the evidence of his family members.
No independent witness has supported the prosecution case.
There are lot of contradiction, omissions and improvement in the statement of the prosecutrix.

The trial Court has not properly considered the evidence and wrongly convicted and sentenced the appellants, hence, the appellants be acquitted in the case of conviction is maintained the period of the sentence be limited to the period already undergone.
8. Learned Panel Lawyer for the State has supported the judgment and submitted that the appeal is without merit, hence, be dismissed.
9. I have gone through the record of the trial Court.

Trial Court after appreciation of the evidence has found that the victim was married and major at the time of the incident and this fact has not been challenged by the State filing by the cross appeal.

Looking to the statement of Dr. Azad Jain (PW-1) and the statement of victim (PW-2) nothing is on record by that it can be assessed that at the time of incident she was minor and on that the trial Court has acquitted the appellant for the offence punishable under Section 363 of the IPC.

sentences.text: The victim (PW-2) in her statement has clearly stated that on the date 4 CRA-1291-2009 of incident at 3 PM, she was going to her uncle's home to bring the bucket for washing her cloths and when she reached near the house of appellant No.2 Shravan, appellant No.1 Anand and appellant No.2 Shravan were standing there and appellant No.1 Anand with the intention to molest her caught hold her and by force brought her in the house of appellant No.2 Shravan.
The appellant No.2 Shravan put the latches of the door from the out side.
Appellant No.2 Shravan dashed down her and tried to rape her.

She cried for help at that time her brother Raghu (PW-4) and Mahendra (PW-3)
reached there, they opened latches of the door and rescued her, if they would have not reached there, appellant No.1 Anand would have committed rape upon her.
11. She narrated the whole story to her brother, father and lodged the FIR (Ex.P-2).
She was medically examined.
In the elaborate cross-examination of this witness nothing has been brought that makes her statement doubtful or untrustworthy.

The witness Mahendra (PW-3) who is the independent witness PW-3 has supported the story that when he heard the cry of victim, he along with Raghu (PW-4) went on the house and opened the gate and they saw that the appellant No.1 Anand tried to rape the victim.
This fact is also supported by the Raghu (PW-4) and Bhim (PW-5).
Bansilal (PW-6) has also supported that the victim told the incident to him.
12. The FIR as proved by Kishor Kumar (PW-8) was lodged on the same day on 30.011.2007 at 5 PM within two hours from the time of the incident.

The distance of the Police Station to the place of incident was 12 KM.
13.

Trial Court has elaborately considered the fact that the accused has dashed down the victim but he has not tried to rape upon the victim as he has not opened the under garments or his cloths as of the victim.

Hence, trial Court 5 CRA-1291-2009 has acquitted the appellants for the offence attempt to rape and the trial Court has elaborately discussed the fact that the appellant No.1 Anand caught hold the victim, brought her into the house of appellant No.2 Shravan.

No one was in the house and house was closed by the appellant No.2 from the out side and in that situation when no other person was present in the house, the intention of the appellant No.1 was clear to outrage the modesty of a woman and on that basis the trial Court has convicted the appellant for the offence punishable under Section 354 of the IPC.

14. To constitute the offence of abduction as per Section 362 of the IPC whoever by force compels, or by any deceitful means induces any person to go from any place, is said to be abducted that person.

Thus, constitute the offence in this case, appellant No.1 Anand has caught hold the victim and by force brought her into the house of the appellant No.2 Shravan for committing the illicit intercourse.

Though the trial Court after appreciation of the evidence has found that the appellant only guilty for the offence punishable under Section 354 of the IPC but the accused has not submitted any explanation for which purpose he by force took the victim into the house of appellant No.2 Shravan.

This fact is proved beyond reasonable doubt from the evidence of the victim and Mahendra (PW-3)
and Raghu (PW-4) that the victim was found into the house of the appellant No.1 Shravan and accused was also present there, he dashed down the victim.
Thus, it is clearly established that the intention of the appellant was to commit illicit intercourse with the victim.

sentences.text: This Court considered the fact that the victim has admitted in Para -6 of her cross-examination that the work of flooring was going on and the pieces of tiles were lying there and floor was uneven and Dr. Sanjeev Dixit (PW-7) who has examined the victim has not found any injury over the body of the 6 CRA-1291-2009 victim but from the evidence of the prosecution the defence failed to probabilize that they have falsely been implicated or create the doubt over the mind of trial Court as well as this Court that the appellant has not dashed down the victim.
16. It is clear from the evidence of the victim that when the appellant No.1 Anand brought the victim into the house of the appellant No.2 Shravan, the house was locked from the outside.
The witness Mahendra (PW-3) has clearly stated that when they reached on the spot they saw that the gate of the house was closed from outside.

This fact is also supported by Raghu (PW-4) and he has also stated that the door of the house was closed from the outside and the appellant No.2 was trying to molest the victim and just after incident, the victim has narrated the story to her father and the uncle Bansilal (PW-6) and from the evidence of the victim it is also clear that when she was going towards uncle Bansilal's home to bring the Bucket, the appellants were standing in front of their house and appellant No.1 Anand caught hold her and by the force brought into the house of the appellant No.2 Shravan and the door was closed from the outside by putting the latches, no other person was present over there.

The house belongs to the appellant No.2 Shravan and appellant No.1 was standing outside just before the incident and naturally it be inferred that appellant No.2 Shravan has closed the door by putting the latch on the door and confined the victim in the room
, thus the offence of Section 342 is also proved.
17. Thus, this Court affirms the conviction of the appellant No.1 Anand under Sections 366, 354 and 342 of the IPC.
In the same way the conviction of the appellant No.2 Shravan under Section 342 of the IPc is also maintained.

18. Considered on the sentence, in this case, the trial Court looking to the 7 CRA-1291-2009 tender age of the appellant No.1 Anand has called the report of the Probation Officer Khandwa on conviction dated 22.06.2009 and after that the sentence was passed on 03.07.2009.
Thus, after considering the report of the Probation Officer, sentenced the appellant No.1.

The offence punishable under Section 366 is punishable with the imprisonment of either description for a term which may extent to 10 years and also the fine and for the offence punishable under Section 354 at that time offence was committed, punishable sentenced upto 2 years or with fine or with both and for the offence punishable under Section 342 with the imprisonment of either description which may extent to 1 year or with fine which may extend to Rs.1000/- or with both.

19. I have considered the fact, in this case, looking to the period of the pendency of the appeal and the sentence passed against the appellant No.2 Shravan offence punishable under Section 342 of the IPC is altered and in place of imprisonment the appellant for the offence punishable under Section 342 in place of 1 years R.I., the appellant No.2 Shravan shall deposit Rs.1000/-, default in depositing the amount, if not already deposited, appellant No.2 shall under go for simple imprisonment of 3 months.

sentences.text: The jail sentence of appellant No.1 Anand for offence under Section 342 of the IPC is altered from jail sentence to fine only and he shall deposit the fine amount of Rs.1000/-, in default, he shall undergo imprisonment of 3 months.
For the offence punishable under Section 366 in place of 4 years his jail sentence is reduced to the period of 1 year and fine amount is enhanced to Rs.5000/-.
For the offence punishable under Section 354, the appellant shall ungergo R.I. for 1 year and fine amount of Rs.5000/-.
If the fine amount is not deposited, he shall further undergo four months of R.I. for each default.
21. The fine already deposited shall be adjusted.
The fine amount shall be 8 CRA-1291-2009 deposited within three months from today.

22. The appellant No.1 Anand s/o Babulal shall surrender before the trial Court within two weeks from the date of the order of this Court and trial Court shall prepare the supersession warrant and sent the appellant to undergo the rest of jail sentence.
The period of detention during the trial shall be set off.
23. The punishment of the jail sentence shall run concurrently and the jail sentence in default of the depositing the fine shall run consecutively.
The bail bonds of the appellants are discharged.
24. With the copy of the judgment, the record of the trial Court be returned back for necessary information and compliance.
25. Record of this appeal be consigned to record room.
